title: Recovered posts across time
basis: 277 records and the original 235 caption sample
analysis: The expanded dataset contains 277 records, including 21 additional authored posts found in the signed-in browser. All 256 activities in the original package were checked individually. The large 2026 total describes the recovered sample; it does not establish a change in the account’s actual publishing frequency.
note: Counts include reposts and additions. Zero means no recovered record. Grey cells fall outside March 2023 to September 2026. Additions use displayed dates; original dates use UTC. Annual medians below use only the original 235 eligible captions.

title: Reactions and comments over time
analysis: Reactions and comments follow different paths. In the original caption sample, the annual median was 86 reactions and 2 comments in 2024, 69 and 4 in 2025, and 54 and 3 in January to September 2026. Recent posts have had less time to accumulate public response, so this pattern cannot establish a decline in reach.
note: Quarterly medians. Periods with fewer than three captions are suppressed. Counts are cumulative values preserved from the supplied package.

title: The monthly response calendar
analysis: Monthly variation gives useful places to investigate individual posts. A strong month may reflect a conference or just a small group of recovered activities. Compare the counts printed in each cell before treating a difference as a trend. The reaction and comment calendars use separate colour scales.
note: Cell labels show median and n. Cells with fewer than three captions show only n. Blank cells outside the audit window are not observations.

title: Longer captions and more AI mentions
analysis: Median caption length rose from 86 words in 2024 to 296 in 2026, while explicit AI mentions rose from 24 percent to 63 percent. This is a shift in the observed editorial mix. It supports making each post’s particular decision easier to identify, rather than assuming that length itself is the cause of response.
note: 2026 covers January to September. AI means the supplied explicit AI or artificial intelligence indicator, including hashtags. Word counts include links and hashtags.

title: Monthly length and public response
basis: Months with at least 3 eligible captions
analysis: Across monthly medians, the supplied rank correlation is −0.27 for length and reactions and 0.42 for length and comments. These associations move in different directions. Year, topic, audience exposure and post age change at the same time, so shortening a caption cannot be expected to produce a specific response lift.
note: Each bubble is a month. Bubble area represents the number of eligible captions. These are monthly comparisons, not estimates of individual post effects.

title: Ten posts to study closely
analysis: Finance occupies five of the top ten positions. These posts make concrete constraints visible: capital, climate finance, debt and project delivery. Clean cooking appears twice. The leading resource-sharing post also shows that a link can coexist with strong public response. This is a collection of examples to study, not proof of a preferred format.
note: The original score averages reaction and comment percentile ranks with equal weight. Ranks are preserved, including tie breaks. Public counts are not engagement rates.

title: Topic mix and share of discussion
analysis: AI and digital systems are the largest primary topic group. The comparison between post share and comment share reveals where discussion is disproportionately concentrated within this sample. A larger comment share can be driven by a few exceptional posts; it is not an exposure-adjusted measure of topic performance.
note: Each caption has one primary topic. Post shares and comment shares have different denominators. All eight topics are shown, including Other.

title: Topic attention and discussion
basis: Topic groups with at least 5 eligible captions
analysis: Technology and grids have medians of 74 reactions and 4 comments. Finance has 72 and 3; AI and digital has 62 and 3. The comment medians are close, and distributions overlap. Use topic comparisons to identify editorial questions worth testing, rather than treating small median differences as a definitive ranking.
note: Bubble area is the number of captions. Dashed lines mark overall caption medians of 68 reactions and 3 comments. Labels are displaced for readability, with leaders to their points.

title: Writing approach and relative response
analysis: Event reporting has medians of 74 reactions and 4 comments, compared with 56 and 1 for event invitations. Insight posts have medians of 66 and 3. The practical opportunity is to report what was learned, disputed or decided at an event. This observational comparison does not isolate the effect of writing approach.
note: Response index divides each group median by the overall median, then multiplies by 100. Groups with fewer than five captions are suppressed in the response panel.

title: Reactions by topic and approach
analysis: The intersections separate subject from writing approach. Dense cells support closer comparisons; sparse cells reveal where the record cannot support a reliable generalisation. Use these intersections to choose matched tests on the same subject instead of comparing unrelated posts.
note: Each cell shows median reactions and n. A median requires at least three captions. All topics and all six approaches are retained.

title: Comments by topic and approach
analysis: Read the comment matrix alongside the reaction matrix. A combination that attracts visible appreciation may not produce discussion. The many small groups make it especially important to inspect the underlying captions and comments before adopting an editorial rule.
note: Each cell shows median comments and n. A median requires at least three captions. The colour scale is specific to comments.

title: Approach differences within each year
analysis: The event-reporting advantage remains visible in 2026: its medians are 66 reactions and 3.5 comments, against 49 and 3 for insight posts. Comparing within a year removes one broad source of distortion, but does not control for subject, audience, format or post age.
note: Cells show medians and counts. Fewer than three captions suppresses the median. All six approaches appear; 2026 is January to September.

title: How topics become different kinds of posts
analysis: The flow diagram shows the editorial choices available within each topic. Its ribbon widths sum to all 235 eligible captions. A subject such as finance can become an argument, a report from negotiations or a resource. The useful decision is which form makes the substantive issue clearest.
note: Ribbon width is caption count. Every caption has one primary topic and one dominant approach. These are editorial flows, not audience journeys.

title: Topics that appear together
analysis: Co-mentions suggest series that connect related professional questions, such as AI financing or digital infrastructure in island systems. The network uses the original keyword tags and retains the original six tracked topic families. It describes language in captions; it is not a map of causal or organisational relationships.
note: Node area represents tagged caption count. Only the ten strongest co-mentions are drawn. A caption can contribute to multiple nodes and edges.

title: Individual response and its concentration
analysis: The top 25 original activities account for about 32 percent of comments and 23 percent of reactions when ranked separately for each measure. A small number of discussions therefore contribute a substantial part of the observed total. This supports studying exceptional posts alongside the median, while keeping their individual contexts visible.
note: Left shows each original activity. Right ranks separately by each counter. The diagonal is equal response per post. Public totals do not reveal unique participants.

title: Question marks and yearly response
analysis: A question mark alone is not associated with a higher yearly median comment count in this record. In 2025 and 2026 the medians are the same for captions with and without questions; in 2024, captions with questions have a lower median. The editorial test should concern the substance of a question, not its mere presence.
note: Question presence means at least one question mark anywhere in the caption. Counts and medians are descriptive and do not measure question quality.

title: Similar text can receive different response
basis: Two selected pairs of original activities
analysis: The crisis-setting captions are identical but received 14 and 23 reactions. The two UNGA invitations differ slightly in formatting and tagging and received 89 and 59. Both pairs remain separate activities. Exposure, timing and audience can vary even when the writing changes little; two examples cannot establish a repetition penalty.
note: The pairs are selected examples from the source report. Reactions use a common scale within each pair; comment counts are printed beside them.

title: What the expanded audit establishes
analysis: All 256 original activities received a browser check. The expanded collection holds 267 nonempty author captions and 276 locally saved main visuals. Full-account completeness remains unknown. Twenty of the 21 additions still lack a resolved activity ID, and exact UTC publication times remain unresolved for all 21 additions.
note: Coverage measures overlap and have different denominators. They must not be added. Missing visible counters are unknown, not zero. Visuals include selected video stills and document covers.

title: Every recovered post in chronological order
basis: All 277 records including one no-image record
analysis: The chronology makes the visual record inspectable from the earliest recovered post to the latest. Each tile preserves the source aspect ratio and carries the dataset index. The one record without a standalone visual remains visible as a labelled placeholder, so the mosaic does not silently lose a post.
note: All 277 dataset indices occur once. Images are previews of the saved originals. Click a tile in the HTML for the caption, source and full-size image. Tiny print thumbnails are an index, not a substitute for the digital gallery.

title: The complete visual record by topic
analysis: Grouping images by primary topic makes repeated visual treatments easier to spot. The 21 additions remain explicitly unclassified because their topic coding has not been reconciled with the original scheme. Their presence should not be mistaken for a new editorial topic.
note: All indices occur once. Topic labels are inherited editorial classifications. Within each topic, tiles follow publication date and preserve image aspect ratio.

title: The colour character of the archive
basis: 276 saved visuals and one no-image record
analysis: The palette atlas is an exploratory view of recurring colour treatments. Blue and cyan accents dominate the computed groups, but photographs, slides and branded covers can share similar palettes. Colour grouping describes pixels and cannot establish visual quality, subject matter or audience preference.
note: Grouping uses the dominant saturated hue in a small image sample, with light and dark neutral categories. Original images are not recoloured or cropped.

title: The leading posts as a visual collection
basis: Top 24 of 246 rankable original activities · R reactions · C comments
analysis: The leading collection combines images with preserved ranks and separate reaction and comment counts. It is useful for examining what readers actually encountered: documents, event photographs and covers all appear. The selection alone cannot determine which visual format caused the response.
note: Ranks use the supplied equal-weight percentile score. The same baseline counts are used throughout. Image size is constant as a frame and does not encode performance.

title: Topic distributions beyond the median
analysis: The middle half of each topic’s reaction counts gives context that a single median hides. Wide and overlapping intervals mean that many posts in different topics receive similar response. A strong outlier can coexist with an ordinary median, so topic decisions should combine the distribution with close reading of individual examples.
note: Boxes span the 25th to 75th percentile. A dark dot marks the median; pale points show every caption. Horizontal position is reactions. Vertical jitter is deterministic and has no meaning.

title: Caption features as testable hypotheses
analysis: These comparisons separate opening questions, links, AI mentions and first-person language. The groups are not otherwise matched, and each feature can overlap with the others. Use differences as hypotheses for a controlled editorial test; neither a link nor a personal pronoun is an independent explanation of public response.
note: Paired dots show medians with and without each feature. Counts accompany each comparison. First-person and opening-question indicators use the supplied coding.

title: Individual caption length and response
analysis: The individual-post view exposes the spread hidden by monthly medians. Posts with similar lengths can receive very different response. Length is therefore better treated as an editorial constraint to test within a comparable subject and format than as a universal optimisation target.
note: Each dot is an eligible caption, coloured by year. The two panels preserve the separate reaction and comment outcomes. No fitted causal relationship is implied.

title: What kinds of main visuals were saved
analysis: The saved asset types help plan future visual work and identify what is still missing. A video cover or still is represented by one image, and a document by its cover. This collection supports a main-visual audit, but it does not represent the full narrative of a video, document or carousel.
note: Counts describe the asset selected for this archive. They are not necessarily LinkedIn post-format classifications. One record has no standalone visual.

title: All tracked topic co-mentions
analysis: The matrix expands the network into every pair among the six original keyword-tag families. This exposes weaker connections that a top-ten network omits. The diagonal gives each tag’s total; off-diagonal values count captions containing both tags. Frequent co-mention is a starting point for reading, not evidence of strategic importance.
note: Multi-label keyword tags can overlap. The matrix is symmetric and should not be summed as a count of unique posts.

title: Original and browser counters compared
analysis: The browser audit found 37 counter differences across 37 records. Both snapshots are retained because the cause of a difference is not established. A lower visible total can reflect a changed count or a difference in what the interface displays. Mixing these newer values into the original ranking would create an inconsistent comparison.
note: Each row shows the signed browser-minus-package difference. Labels identify the dataset index and counter. Zero is the agreement reference; omitted records did not yield a recorded difference.

title: A practical sequence of editorial tests
basis: Proposed tests rather than measured outcomes
analysis: Start with subjects already present in the record and change one editorial choice at a time. Pair a concise argument with a concrete visual, compare event reporting with an invitation on a similar topic, and test a specific professional question. Record impressions and response at the same post age where account analytics are available.
note: This is a proposed workflow, not a performance forecast. Keep topic, audience and timing as comparable as practical. Review substantive comments as well as counts.

title: The shapes of the visual archive
analysis: Aspect ratios determine how much text and detail remain legible in a feed. This view separates portrait, near-square and landscape assets while retaining the original shapes. It can guide a more consistent production system, but the archive does not support a claim that one aspect ratio increases reach.
note: Portrait is width/height below 0.9, near-square is 0.9 to 1.1, and landscape is above 1.1. Counts refer to saved main visuals, not all assets in each post.
